runs.question: Does the command runner terminate its child process group on timeout and report that execution as unsuccessful? Review only this process-lifecycle boundary.
reasons: Source evidence does not match the recorded file/line

runs.question: Does the command runner terminate its owned process group on timeout or cancellation and report that execution as unsuccessful? Review this boundary only; escaped independent process groups and whole-program acceptance are excluded.

reviewer.head: 933452554216b791a30efc1691677c4871af7b31
reviewer.summary: Cancellation can be missed while the command log is being opened. Timeout handling otherwise targets the owned process group and marks execution unsuccessful.

findings.title: Recheck cancellation after asynchronous log setup
findings.consequence: If the signal is aborted during log setup, the initial check has already passed and the abort listener is registered too late to receive the event. The command then starts and can finish with code 0 and cancelled=false, which requireSuccess accepts. Otherwise it continues until its timeout instead of terminating promptly on cancellation.

evidence.quote: if (signal?.aborted) return { code: null, cancelled: true, stdout: '', stderr: '', elapsedMs: 0 };

const abort = () => { cancelled = true; stop(); };
    signal?.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });

runs.question: Does the selected canonical result parser preserve delivered numbers and reject unsupported types without falling back to raw input?

reviewer.head: 556f35d6708f28ec32659a9f25a5ab5e80c268a4
reviewer.summary: No actionable findings. The parser preserves delivered numeric values and comparators and rejects unsupported value types without reconstructing values from raw input. All 24 contract tests passed. The synthetic FHIR roundtrip failed during certificate authentication and provides no evidence about parser behavior.

scope: Harness integration acceptance; not current application stack clearance or a reviewer-quality benchmark. L2 findings were separately reproduced by failing tests and fixed in the implementation. The failed FHIR fixture was corrected; rerun pending.
